title: Complete optical appearance accounts constrained by reflection and point correspondence
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. A variable whole account may distinguish eye, object, mirror and apparent image through shared laws relating all corresponding points. Catoptrics19 supplies a complete proof and owned modern diagram: image size, opposite-side placement and perpendicular-distance equality jointly constrain a mirror reading, while a180-degree-rotation rival can preserve size but exchange point correspondence. No optical meaning is assigned to the earlier formal array-reflection result.

design.mechanism: A prospective globally shared language declares geometric objects and relations, observer and object roles, visibility conditions, apparent locations, and proof assertions. Plane reflection is one fixed operation applied consistently to all corresponding points: perpendicular-foot preservation, opposite signed distances and equal pairwise lengths. More complicated texts may add multiple objects or observations without changing the operation. Only explicit alternative branches may change a hypothesis. This describes optical content rather than a free JOIN/CIRCLE drawing program.
design.unit: A whole owned optical claim, setup, construction, argument and conclusion, including prerequisite calls and visible figure ownership. No number of source steps or symbols is equated with target paragraph length; a variable whole-text grammar and its morphological alternatives remain unspecified.
design.contrast: GDT221 did not transfer its construction-to-record assignment; that missing owner is not solved by an optical name. GDT796 retains only a narrow unstable formal relative-reflection texture with no general status/word code. Its primary was read; no f71 optical owner or mirror word is inferred from it. IDEA000125 is generic geometric construction, while this proposal requires observer/object/apparent-location roles with physical reflection consequences beyond arbitrary auxiliary geometry.
design.prediction: For a fixed mirror and shared point references, every image point must lie on its own object perpendicular at opposite signed distance. A same-side copy preserves lengths but violates side; a180-degree rotation can preserve lengths and place the image opposite while exchanging perpendicular feet. The model must distinguish these globally, rather than rename each ray or reflection locally. A future target test needs explicitly hypothesized but independently checkable mirror/object/image ownership. Mere circles or mirrored list order are insufficient.
